DC.wall: Glass curtain wall, green/teal-tinted, on a long barrel-vaulted (curved-top) form
DC.secondary: Low wings in beige/tan precast panels with horizontal metal banding (#a69c90); silver corrugated metal panel walls; bright red painted steel portal frames at entrances; teal-grey ductwork 'elbows' arching over the vault
DC.features: Not brick, not concrete: a high-tech 1988 glass vault. Big teal ducts loop over the curved glass roof edge; red steel frames/columns at the plaza entrances. Plaza in front is red-brown/grey interlocking brick pavers.

MC.wall: Raw board-marked / finely fluted grey concrete, brutalist
MC.secondary: Small amount of brown brick infill at ground level; dark window frames
MC.features: 1968 brutalist block on pilotis: upper floors cantilever over a recessed ground floor on heavy concrete piers; tall blank windowless concrete stair/service towers (where the giant pink tie is hung); upper floors have repetitive small vertical window openings with concrete fins forming continuous bands.

M3.secondary: Curtain wall in a checker of pale teal/aqua, clear and dark-blue glass panels with silver mullions; white top band/parapet
M3.features: 2018 4-storey box: brick 'bookend' piers framing a large mixed-tint glass grid centre facade; glazed bridge to MC; narrow vertical glass slots on the brick returns.

QNC.wall: Reflective silver/blue glass curtain wall with vertical mullion fins
QNC.secondary: Base podium of dark charcoal/grey brick in mixed tones (#4f4f4f); white/light grey panel band above the podium
QNC.features: 2012. Two volumes: a long glass bar with strong vertical fins cantilevering over the entrance, plus a glass cube clad in a hexagonal 'honeycomb' frame. Ground-floor accents in orange-red. NOT copper - no copper panels seen in any photo.

SLC.wall: Curved blue glass ribbon facade (courtyard side) with grey metal spandrel bands
SLC.secondary: Red-brown brick end pavilions (#8b5a40); buff split-face concrete block piers carrying a brown timber pergola; grey metal siding upper level. 2020s SLC/PAC expansion: green-tinted glass with vertical fins over white precast columns
SLC.features: Crescent-shaped courtyard facade wrapping a paved plaza with picnic tables; pergola walkways. The new expansion on the PAC side is a glass box on a white colonnade.

PAC.secondary: Dark grey/charcoal sloped metal roofs and fascias; 2020s expansion in glass curtain wall + grey metal panels with black Warriors logo
PAC.features: 1970 sports complex: large flat white membrane roof over the main gym ringed by lower dark-grey sloped/stepped roofs; gabled clerestory entrance pavilion in brown brick; few windows on the old part.

LIB.wall: White/cream precast concrete fins (vertical ribs) on the tower
LIB.secondary: Dark brown fascia band between tower and podium (#5a4636); podium in cream precast with a band of round-arched glazing at ground level
LIB.features: Dana Porter 'sugar cube': 10-storey near-cubic tower with closely spaced vertical precast fins and narrow vertical window slots, sitting on a wider 2-storey podium; the tower overhangs on a recessed dark band. Ground floor has distinctive arched (vaulted) openings.

HH.secondary: SAF wing (2010s): darker purple-brown brick (#6f5848), taupe/bronze metal panels, glass curtain wall at entrance
HH.features: Brick, not concrete. The Humanities Theatre fly tower is a huge nearly windowless brown-brick block with a clerestory strip at the top. The newer School of Accounting & Finance addition has horizontal strip windows set in brick and a full-glass upper storey.

ML.secondary: Concrete/precast trim and stair; grey window frames
ML.features: Long low brick walls animated by tall narrow angled vertical window slots (vertical strip windows); faces the Arts Quad. Theatre of the Arts inside.

E5.wall: Silver/light grey faceted (pleated, diamond-pattern) metal panel cladding
E5.secondary: Horizontal glass ribbon bands; dark charcoal metal-clad base volume; glazed bridge to E7/DC across Ring Road
E5.features: 2011 6-storey box with prismatic shimmering silver panels in a zig-zag pattern; long glazed pedestrian bridge.

E6.wall: Dark navy/charcoal glass and panel grid
E6.features: Dark blue-black facade of glass and opaque panels in a staggered/random rhythm of window sizes; reads as a dark monolith next to E5.

E7.secondary: White/silver pleated (faceted) metal panels similar to E5; round raw-concrete columns
E7.features: 2018, renamed Pearl Sullivan Engineering Building. Large glass mass with a deep overhang on cylindrical concrete columns at the entrance; faceted white panel sections; red stairs visible through glass in the atrium.

EIT.secondary: Light blue-green glass curtain wall sections, white/silver metal panels and sunshades
EIT.features: 2003 Teeple Architects. Crisp modernist blocks of buff brick with large glazed corners and projecting glass bays.

STC.secondary: Dark grey/charcoal metal panels; glazed bridges
STC.features: 2021 Science Teaching Complex: glass and brick, bridged to neighbouring science buildings; blue interior accents visible through glass.

EV1.features: 1970s Environment 1; not clearly identified in photos I could view. Interior atrium shows buff brick and raw concrete.

EV2.features: Low brick building adjacent to EV3; a Commons view near EV3 shows a 2-storey red-brick block next to the lime/grey EV3 cladding, which is probably EV2/EV1.

EV3.wall: Light grey/taupe and dark grey rainscreen panels with lime-green horizontal stripes
EV3.features: 2011 LEED Platinum. Strong horizontal banding of lime green; roof largely covered in solar panels plus green roof (reads blue-grey from above).

V1.secondary: Grey concrete paver roof terraces; brown/dark window frames
V1.features: Village 1 (1965): central complex plus clusters of 2-3 storey flat-roofed brick 'houses' around green courtyards connected by paths. Some green roofs on the central building.

REV.secondary: Silver/grey aluminium entrance pavilion; window/spandrel bands
REV.features: 3-4 storey brick residence wings with long horizontal window rows; formerly 'Village 2'.

PHY.features: 1960s 4-storey long slab with dense horizontal rows of windows (punched windows reading as bands); a small white observatory dome on the roof.

CPH.secondary: Concrete; brick planters with red-painted wooden benches
CPH.features: Carl Pollock Hall: low buff-brick engineering block, outdoor seating terrace with pergola.

B1.wall: Unknown - likely 1960s concrete/precast with brick (not verified)
B1.features: Could not find a clearly labelled exterior photo. A university Biology page shows a concrete building raised on pilotis with a window grid, probably B1/B2.

C2.wall: Unknown - likely 1960s precast concrete/buff brick (not verified)

ESC.secondary: Raw concrete columns; rooftop lab mechanical units
ESC.features: 3-storey block with continuous horizontal window bands (archival department-history photo); 2024 photos show raw concrete column/beam details at the entrance.

NH.wall: Dark red-brown brick (original); orange-red brick on 2015 expansion
NH.secondary: Expansion: glass curtain wall, white/silver metal panels, glazed bridge
NH.features: Original 1970s Needles Hall is a chunky stepped brick block; the 2015 expansion adds a brighter orange-red brick volume with large glass sections and a bridge.

DWE.wall: Buff/tan brick with darker speckled bricks
DWE.secondary: Concrete band courses; aluminium windows; black canopy
DWE.features: Douglas Wright Engineering: plain 1950s-60s buff brick block with grouped window panels.

E2.secondary: Dark navy/charcoal metal fascia band; glass entrance additions
E2.features: Low red-brick engineering building with a dark metal roof band; newer glazed entrance.

E3.wall: Unknown exterior; interior bay is raw concrete
E3.secondary: Silver corrugated metal siding and buff split-face block on adjacent lab wing (ECH)
E3.features: Commons interior photo shows raw concrete columns and perforated concrete balcony fronts with red/yellow steel. Exterior not verified.

RCH.features: J.R. Coutts Engineering Lecture Hall; 2009 Daily Bulletin photo shows brick with modern glazed additions. Low confidence on details.

AL.wall: Light grey/white concrete with vertical blade walls/fins
AL.secondary: Dark brown brick base; dark glazing
AL.features: Arts Lecture Hall: monumental, fortress-like; repetitive vertical concrete fins (an Instagram architecture post compares it to ancient Egyptian buildings); faces Dana Porter across the Arts Quad, wide concrete steps.

PAS.secondary: Brown brick tower/stair volumes (#7a5a48); recessed dark window bands
PAS.features: Stepped/terraced 1960s brutalist block with deep horizontal window bands and concrete spandrels; brick towers at one end.

TC.secondary: Glass curtain wall corner/entrance volumes; dark metal
TC.features: Tatham Centre (2002): long 3-storey block with a dark red brick main facade, strip windows, and fully glazed end/entrance pavilions.

GSC.features: General Services Complex: low utilitarian brick buildings with the campus's tall brick chimney, a landmark.

SCH.secondary: White/light concrete upper bands and parapets
SCH.features: South Campus Hall: stepped, terraced massing with white horizontal bands over brown brick; faces University Ave entrance.

TJB.features: Toby Jenkins Applied Health Research Building: glass box with white panel frame; signage on a white band.

BMH.features: Applied Health Sciences complex (BMH/LHI/LHN); thumbnails show brick and glass; could not separate buildings with confidence.

LHI.features: Lyle Hallman Institute; see BMH note.

MKV.secondary: Grey/white precast panels; rounded glazed stair tower
MKV.features: Mackenzie King Village: 4-5 storey brick residence with light precast bays and a cylindrical stair tower.

UWP.wall: Light buff/greyish brick (towers); buff/cream brick low courts
UWP.features: UW Place: ~11-12 storey slab towers (Beck/Eby halls etc.) plus low-rise courtyard buildings (Wellesley, Waterloo, Woolwich Courts).

CLV.secondary: Beige/grey vinyl siding upper floors; grey asphalt shingle pitched roofs
CLV.features: Columbia Lake Village: suburban 2-storey townhouse rows with pitched roofs.

CMH.secondary: Darker brick accent bands; white/silver metal and glass base
CMH.features: Claudette Millar Hall: ~16-18 storey brick residence tower (Masri O Architects) on a glazed podium.

FED.features: Federation Hall: low 1-storey brick hall with sloped roof sections near Ring Road. Low confidence on details.

GH.secondary: Dark brown hip roof shingles, brown shutters and wooden porch
GH.features: Graduate House: 19th-century 2-storey farmhouse (white walls, brown shutters, arched ground-floor window) - stands out completely from the modern campus.

UC.features: University Club: low single-storey brick building near Village 1.

OPT.secondary: 2009 addition: white/silver metal panels with horizontal frosted/blue glass bands; new Waterloo Eye Institute (2020s) in dark charcoal metal
OPT.features: Original 2-3 storey brick block with horizontal windows, extended by a long sleek white horizontal-banded wing.

CIF.wall: Red-brown brick and white/grey metal siding
CIF.secondary: Red-painted steel structure/canopies; 2023 Field House in grey metal with a huge gold/yellow (#f2b70f) panel and black Warrior logo
CIF.features: Columbia Icefield: low arena/gym complex, large flat roofs; field house addition is a big grey shed with gold branding.

ION_UW.wall: Station tower clad in checker panels of navy, grey-green and white glass
ION_UW.secondary: Glass and steel canopy shelters with dark grey frames; concrete platform with yellow tactile edge
ION_UW.features: University of Waterloo ION LRT station on the rail corridor beside E5/E7 and DC; single sign tower with ION and GRT logos.
